quote.translation: Hegel's view is that arbitrariness, at the lower stage of the will, must be developed into freedom at the higher stage (Hegel, En-cyklopädie, hrsg. v. Bolland, 1906, § 145, Zusatz, S. 194).

regions.text: 我々は自由の概念に開して消極約自由を積極的自由の二つに分けて考へることが出来る。

quote.translation: We can divide the concept of freedom into two, negative freedom and positive freedom.

regions.text: さうすれば、消極的自由とは因果的偶然としての非決定性、自獎性に當ら、横極約自由とは目前々必然としてのヘーゲルの謂はゆる自由に鶯る。

quote.translation: Negative freedom then corresponds to indeterminacy and spontaneity as causal contingency, and positive freedom to what Hegel calls freedom, as teleological necessity.

regions.text: ニョライハルトマンの様相性の研究によれば海極的自由は一または他に行動する可能性であつて、必然性を越えた可能性の優勢である。

quote.translation: According to Nicolai Hartmann's study of Modality, negative freedom is the possibility of acting one way or the other, the predominance of possibility over necessity.

regions.text: 然るに、道德の本質である當爲は可能性を越えた必然性の優勢であるから當爲によつて制約された活動は消極的意味に於て自由であるとは云へない。積極約意味に於て自由といふことが云へるのである。消極的自由は可能性の自由」（FreihcitderMiglich-keit）すなはち「必然性からの

quote.translation: The ought, however, which is the essence of morality, is the predominance of necessity over possibility, so that activity conditioned by the ought cannot be called free in the negative sense; it can be called free in the positive sense.

quote.translation: Negative freedom is "freedom of possibility" (Freiheit der Möglichkeit), that is, "freedom from necessity" (Freiheit „von" der Notwendigkeit), whilst positive freedom, as "freedom from possibility" (Freiheit „von" der Möglichkeit), must be "freedom of necessity" (Freiheit der Notwendigkeit).

quote.translation: Hartmann holds that the freedom of necessity is necessity gushing forth freely, and so arrives at the paradoxical concept of "free necessity" (freie Notwendigkeit) (see N. Hartmann, Logische und ontologische Wirklichkeit, Kantstudien XX, S. 23-24; N. Hartmann, Ethik, 1926, S. 587-589).
